title: WS4: build the hands-free command acceptance corpus
body:
## Priority 1 — start here
Create `evals/voice-commands/cases.json` and `evals/voice-commands/README.md`: a provider-independent acceptance corpus for the first hands-free slice and later Deep Agents. This is expected behavior, not a rewrite of the parser.

Include at least 60 uniquely identified cases: record/select kick, snare and hats; melodic track selection/recording; stop recording versus stop playback; immediate clear/undo; mute, tempo, describe/refine/audition/accept/cancel. Include recording/idle/armed context, realistic paraphrases and at least 15 ambiguous, unsupported or non-command cases. During recording, distinguish recognized Groove commands from singing/beatboxing and ordinary speech. An unrecognized Groove command still excludes its span and produces no mutation. Keep expected musical operations consistent with PLAN.md and the actual contracts; represent clarification/no-op/unsupported explicitly, never invent a wire operation.

Each case: id, context, utterance, expected outcome/operation and arguments when applicable, rationale, and requirement reference. Include multi-turn sound-refinement examples with explicit prior state. Mark future Deep Agents cases separately from phrases expected of the current parser.

### Done when
- JSON parses, IDs are unique, coverage counts are reported.
- README maps cases to requirements and explains how WS3 can consume them; no fake claim that they currently pass.
- No transcripts from private/raw recordings or credentials.

### Fits into the project
WS3 uses this to measure local STT/intent/Deep Agents behavior; WS1 uses it for full-flow acceptance. It can be written offline after reading the repository.

## Working agreement
WS4 owns only `evals/`, `tools/evaluation/`, and `docs/WS4-HANDOFF.md` for these tickets. Do not edit app, service, shared contracts, provider configuration or existing WS3 benchmarks. Read AGENTS.md, PLAN.md, docs/STATUS.md and issue #9 first; fetch and branch from reviewed origin/engine-integration. Submit one focused PR per ticket to engine-integration; WS1 integrates. No API calls, keys, model downloads or raw microphone audio are needed. Use synthetic fixtures where specified and label them synthetic. Leave commit/PR, validation, limitations and next integration step in the handoff. Independent laptop agents must read issue #9 at capability checkpoints; do not dependency-poll.

title: WS4: add a standalone blind-listening results summarizer
body:
## Priority 2 — portable coding task
Create a standard-library-only CLI under `tools/evaluation/` that summarizes the existing blind-listening sheets without running the renderer/models. Inspect PR #13's `research/evaluate.py` and its generated kit/answer-key format (read-only) for exact fields. Do not change WS3's evaluation generator.

Inputs: one kit.json, its separate answer key, and one or more completed sheet.csv files plus their declared kit fingerprint. Produce machine-readable JSON and a readable summary: votes per prompt, A/B/same counts, per-method wins/ties after unblinding, per-listener coverage, missing answers and latency summary if provided. Report raw counts and denominators; do not claim significance or musical quality from embedding scores. Never modify source sheets or place the answer key inside the listener folder.

### Done when
- Reject mismatched fingerprints, invalid preferences, unknown prompt/number pairs, duplicate listener+item rows and malformed answer keys with actionable errors.
- Missing/blank preferences are reported, not counted as ties.
- Deterministic synthetic fixtures verify A/B reversal, ties, incomplete responses and each validation failure. Tests require no dependencies, network, API, models or engine.
- README has a runnable synthetic example and documents the separation of blinded collection from post-collection unblinding.

### Fits into the project
This turns the team's required human listening results into reproducible evidence. Synthetic fixtures prove aggregation only, not actual listening quality.

## Working agreement
WS4 owns only `evals/`, `tools/evaluation/`, and `docs/WS4-HANDOFF.md` for these tickets. Do not edit app, service, shared contracts, provider configuration or existing WS3 benchmarks. title: WS4: freeze held-out sound-description and refinement acceptance cases
body:
## Priority 3 — evaluation design
Create `evals/sound-design/cases.json` and README containing at least 24 new held-out sound-description cases and at least eight refinement conversations. Read PLAN.md and existing WS3 benchmark/tuning prompts first; do not copy those prompts or tune retrieval against this new set.

Cover electric keys, bass, pads, leads, bells/plucks, voice-like textures, and deliberately unsupported requests. Each case includes an ID, natural-language request, target track/context, observable listening criteria (attack/decay, brightness, texture, pitch/timbre, evolution), acceptable variation, and clear pass/partial/fail guidance. Refinements must preserve the composition while changing sound; include audition, accept, cancel and undo. Do not imply editable drums, polyphony or sampling features exist when they do not.

### Done when
- JSON parses, IDs are unique, tuning-prompt overlap is disclosed and avoided.
- Criteria are understandable to a listener and do not depend on an embedding score or preset name.
- README freezes a version and explains how to keep the set held out; subjective results remain blank until real listeners participate.
- No audio generation, model downloads, provider calls or changes to ranking code.

### Fits into the project
WS3/WS1 use this for later sound-retrieval and Deep Agents acceptance. It does not replace the existing shared-kit blind comparison.

## Working agreement
